topic: Change of Basis: Seeing the World Through Different Eyes
target_audience: University students or advanced high school students studying Linear Algebra

sections.title: The Perspective Problem: Two Maps, One Forest
lecture_lines: Coordinates depend on your chosen perspective or basis.
Meet the Human, using a standard North-East grid.
Meet the Owl, using her tilted branch as reference.
A mouse's location looks different to each observer.
Same physical point, but two different sets of coordinates.
animations: Show standard grid (#444444) and tilted grid (#555500) overlapping in the center.
Highlight standard unit vectors i (#FF0000) and j (#00FF00) with 'Human Basis' label.
Highlight tilted unit vectors b1 (#FFFF00) and b2 (#00FFFF) with 'Owl Basis' label.
Place a mouse icon at (3, 2) on the standard grid and label it '(3, 2)' in #FFFFFF.
Scale the mouse icon and show its Owl-basis coordinates; display 'One Point, Two Descriptions' in #00FFFF.

sections.title: Prerequisite Check: What is a Basis?
lecture_lines: A basis is a set of independent spanning vectors.
The standard basis uses unit vectors i and j.
This creates a familiar, rigid square grid.
Vector v is just instructions relative to this grid.
Change the basis, and you change the instructions.
animations: Show two non-parallel vectors b1 (#FFFF00) and b2 (#00FFFF) starting from the origin.
Display standard unit vectors i (#FF0000) and j (#00FF00) with their respective labels.
Draw a square grid [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/grid.svg] in #444444 aligned with i and j.
Draw vector v = 2i + 3j in #FFFFFF, showing arrows for 2 units right and 3 units up.
Animate the basis vectors rotating and scaling to represent changing reference instructions [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/instructions.svg].

sections.title: The 'Dictionary': The Transition Matrix
lecture_lines: A transition matrix translates between different bases.
Describe the Owl's basis vectors using Human coordinates.
These Human-relative vectors become the matrix columns.
Each column translates one basis vector's language.
This matrix acts as our mathematical dictionary.
animations: Display Owl [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/owl.svg]'s basis vectors b1=(1,1) and b2=(-1,1) in #FFFF00 on the standard grid.
Animate the vector coordinates (1,1) and (-1,1) sliding into a 2x2 matrix P.
Label the matrix 'P - Transition Matrix' in #00FFFF above the brackets.
Highlight the first column of P in #FF8800 and the second column in #FF00FF to show they are the basis vectors.
Flash the Owl [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/owl.svg]'s basis vectors to emphasize the matrix-vector relationship.

sections.title: The Mathematical Transformation
lecture_lines: Multiply the matrix to convert coordinates between bases.
Tilted grid lines align with the standard square grid.
The transformation reveals how the other person sees it.
animations: Display the formula '[x]_Human = P * [x]_Owl' in #FFFFFF and highlight the matrix P in #00FFFF.
Show the Owl's tilted grid in #FFFF00 and animate it warping to align with the standard square grid.
Plot a point at (1,1) in Owl-coordinates and show it 'landing' at (0,2) in Human-coordinates; highlight in #00FF00.

sections.title: The Inverse Journey: Going Back
lecture_lines: Use the inverse matrix to return to the original basis.
Change of basis is a two-way mathematical street.
The Human translates his coordinates for the Owl's world.
animations: Display the inverse formula '[x]_Owl = P^-1 * [x]_Human' in #FFFFFF and highlight P^-1 in #00FFFF.
Show a static point on the standard grid and highlight its (x,y) coordinates in #FFFFFF.
Animate the standard grid warping into the Owl's tilted grid #FFFF00 to show the reverse transformation.

sections.title: Summary and Real-World Utility
lecture_lines: Changing the basis doesn't move the physical point.
It simply changes the language used to describe location.
Essential for JPEG compression and computer graphics.
animations: Show a single point with two labels updating simultaneously to show its coordinates in both bases.
Display 'Image Compression' and 'Computer Graphics' in #00FFFF with simple geometric icons.
Fade out all elements and center the text 'Same Vector, Different Basis' in #FFFFFF.
